editorial:
Imagine heading back to your hometown only to find out your dad was keeping a massive secret from everyone. That is exactly what happens to Dr. Sarah Chapel when she returns to Brighton Mills. You will quickly realize that something is very wrong with the locals. Even though they seem healthy, they are all hooked on a drug called Tributol and claim to hear voices while they sleep. The movie feels like a mystery first and a scary flick later, keeping you on your toes as Sarah tries to figure out why her father was treating the whole town like a giant science experiment.

You will love how the mystery builds up, though the pacing slows down a bit in the middle. The acting is solid and makes the weirdness feel real. If you enjoy stories about creepy towns and medical conspiracies, you should definitely give this one a shot. To get the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for those crisp details. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you want something that makes you think while also giving you a few chills.
endingExplained: You find out that the voices are not ghosts, but signals from another dimension. Sarah's father used the drug Tributol to open a door between worlds. In the end, the creatures from the other side try to cross over into our world using the patients as hosts. Sarah has to stop the process to save the town. She manages to shut down the connection, ending the nightmare and finally putting her father's dark experiments to rest.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves medical mysteries and supernatural twists.
